recent_posts.title: NetBox Labs CMDB Integration for ServiceNow Hits the Store with v2.0
recent_posts.summary: NetBox Labs has released v2.0 of its CMDB Integration for ServiceNow, now certified on the ServiceNow Store. The redesigned integration features bidirectional, event-driven sync between NetBox and ServiceNow CMDB, with data stored in an isolated scoped application that doesn't modify core ServiceNow tables. Key capabilities include flexible CI class mapping, full location hierarchy sync, tenant configuration, and support for three sync patterns (NetBox as SOR, ServiceNow as SOR, or hybrid). It supports migration from v1.x, installs via ServiceNow's Application Manager, and is compatible with NetBox Cloud and NetBox Enterprise deployments.

recent_posts.title: New Integrations Extend the NetBox Labs Platform Across the Full Infrastructure Stack
recent_posts.summary: NetBox Labs has released two new generally available integrations for its platform: HPE Juniper Networking Mist (enterprise wireless and campus switching) and Lightyear (WAN circuit procurement and lifecycle management). Additionally, two integrations are entering customer preview: Infoblox NIOS (IPAM/DHCP synchronization) and Cisco ACI (data center fabric discovery). All integrations flow through NetBox Assurance, which stages discovered data as deviations requiring explicit team approval before being committed. Each integration uses a lightweight Docker-based agent requiring only outbound HTTPS. These additions extend the platform to cover enterprise wireless, WAN circuits, IPAM, and data center fabric alongside existing connectors for Cisco Catalyst Center, Cisco Meraki, VMware vCenter, and ServiceNow CMDB.

recent_posts.title: Why the NetBox Labs Platform Is the Foundation for OT Asset Inventory
recent_posts.summary: NetBox Labs positions its platform as the purpose-built system of record for OT asset inventory in utility environments. Unlike IT-centric CMDBs, it models granular device, port, circuit, and physical connectivity data. NetBox Assurance continuously reconciles live network state against documented baselines, supporting NERC CIP compliance controls like CIP-002 and CIP-010. NetBox Discovery integrates with multi-vendor systems (VMware vCenter, Cisco Catalyst Center, Juniper Mist) to automate inventory collection. Together, these capabilities enable NOC modernization, zero-touch provisioning, and data-driven troubleshooting for electric utilities and critical infrastructure operators.

recent_posts.title: Why AI for Infrastructure Fails Without a Semantic Map
recent_posts.summary: AI-powered infrastructure operations often fail not because of weak models, but because AI agents lack semantic context about how infrastructure components relate to each other. A semantic map — a living, machine-readable knowledge graph encoding physical topology, operational context, and configuration relationships — is essential for AI to make informed decisions. NetBox is highlighted as the de facto semantic map for network and infrastructure AI, with its relational data model, MCP server for exposing context to AI agents, and the importance of keeping it current to avoid drift. Teams succeeding with AI invest in rich semantic context rather than chasing more sophisticated LLMs.

recent_posts.title: Bulk Operations at Scale: Introducing NetBox TurboBulk
recent_posts.summary: NetBox Labs is announcing TurboBulk, a high-performance bulk data API for NetBox Cloud and NetBox Enterprise premium tier customers. Unlike the standard REST API which processes objects one at a time through the ORM (typically 100-200 objects/second), TurboBulk operates at the database level using PostgreSQL's native COPY protocol and bulk SQL statements, achieving over 24,000 objects per second. Key features include bulk export in JSONL or Parquet format with a deterministic caching layer (returning HTTP 304 when data hasn't changed), asynchronous write operations with insert/upsert/delete support, three validation modes (None/Auto/Full), dry-run mode, changelog/webhook support, and integration with NetBox Branching. In real-world testing against tens of millions of objects, TurboBulk completed a full export in ~10 minutes vs. an estimated 23+ hours with the REST API, using under 500 MB of memory.

recent_posts.title: NetBox Community Hits 20,000 GitHub Stars
recent_posts.summary: NetBox, the open source network source of truth originally released by DigitalOcean in 2016, has crossed 20,000 GitHub stars. The project now has 391 contributors, 14,904 commits, 3,000+ forks, and 351 releases over a decade. The second 10,000 stars came in just four years, faster than the first. NetBox Labs, the commercial steward, funds core engineering and is building AI-powered products on top of the structured data model, including NetBox Copilot for natural-language infrastructure management. The project is trusted by over 10,000 teams worldwide.

recent_posts.title: See Your Infrastructure: Introducing NetBox Visual Explorer
recent_posts.summary: NetBox Labs is launching NetBox Visual Explorer, a set of interactive visualizations built on top of existing NetBox data. It includes 2D/3D floorplans with importable floor plans, rack elevation views with drag-and-drop editing, power chain tracing for redundancy analysis, cable topology graphs with path highlighting, IP address space visualizations as sunburst or heatmap, and a WAN geo map with circuit arcs. The tool is designed for large-scale environments with thousands of racks and devices. It complements NetBox Copilot (AI assistant) by focusing on the human operator experience for higher-order planning. Currently available as a customer preview for NetBox Cloud customers.

recent_posts.title: Teaching Copilot to Write: How NetBox Copilot Goes Beyond Read-Only
recent_posts.summary: NetBox Copilot now supports write operations (create, update, delete) in addition to read-only queries, available to NetBox Cloud and Enterprise customers. Users can manage infrastructure objects through natural language conversations, with every write requiring explicit human approval before execution. Changes execute under the user's existing session, preserving RBAC policies and audit trails. Future plans include bulk operations and a trust model that shifts toward autonomous routine work with human review only for higher-risk changes.

recent_posts.title: The Long War Against Configuration Chaos
recent_posts.summary: A historical survey of 70 years of infrastructure documentation challenges, from physical binders and spreadsheets through SNMP, CMDBs, and IaC tools, examining why each approach fell short. The core argument is that documentation fails not just due to tooling gaps but due to data model limitations and organizational discipline. The piece concludes by outlining four requirements for a modern system of record—purpose-built data model, API-first design, intent-vs-reality validation, and physical infrastructure support—and positions NetBox as a platform built around these requirements, with particular relevance to AI datacenter environments demanding real-time infrastructure tracking.

recent_posts.title: Understanding Cable Profiles in NetBox 4.5
recent_posts.summary: NetBox 4.5 introduces Cable Profiles, a new optional feature that models the internal channel structure of multi-channel cables such as breakout fanouts, MPO trunks, and polarity shuffle assemblies. Previously, NetBox treated cables as single opaque links; now it can trace specific lanes or fiber pairs through complex cabling topologies. Built-in profiles cover single, trunk, breakout, and shuffle cable types. When a profile is assigned, path tracing becomes per-lane aware, following exact connector and position mappings through each hop. The feature integrates with a new Advanced Port Mappings model for FrontPorts, enabling full end-to-end tracing fidelity through patch panels and inline devices. Cable Profiles are fully backward-compatible and exposed via REST and GraphQL APIs.

top_posts.title: How to Automate Proxmox Virtual Machine Configuration with NetBox and Ansible AWX/Tower/Automation Platform (AAP)
top_posts.summary: NetBox is a popular Network Source of Truth (NSoT) that can be integrated with Proxmox to automate and manage virtual machine (VM) states using Ansible AWX/Tower/Automation Platform (AAP). This integration leverages event-driven automation with webhooks and event rules in NetBox to trigger automated actions in Proxmox using predefined Ansible playbooks. Version 1.1.0 of netbox-proxmox-automation facilitates this setup, requiring a running AWX instance, defined projects, credentials, and job templates. Users must configure necessary scripts and settings to ensure seamless automation.

top_posts.title: 5 Takeaways from 100+ Conversations with CXOs & VPs about Network and Infrastructure Management
top_posts.summary: As 2025 approaches, network and infrastructure management is rapidly evolving. At NetBox Labs, conversations with network and infrastructure leaders have identified five key trends: data-driven operations, aligned observability, incremental automation, secure control, and strategic AI. Organizations that effectively manage their data, integrate observability with intent, adopt step-by-step automation, maintain stringent security controls, and leverage AI strategically are better positioned for success. These insights are shaping the approach and products offered by NetBox Labs to help teams unlock their full potential.

top_posts.title: NetBox Helm Charts 5.0 Is Now Available
top_posts.summary: NetBox Helm Charts 5.0, created initially by Chris Boot, marks a significant milestone with its latest version. This update includes modernized PostgreSQL and Redis subcharts and follows Semantic Versioning for better feature and change management. Upgrading to version 5.0 may require attention to breaking changes, especially for those using built-in PostgreSQL. Future updates will focus on dependencies and configuration customization.

top_posts.title: How to Get Started Using Ansible Tags: A Tutorial
top_posts.summary: Ansible tags provide selective control over task execution in playbooks, allowing developers to run specific tasks or skip others using --tags and --skip-tags flags. The tutorial covers basic tag assignment to tasks, special tags like 'always' and 'never' for conditional execution, applying tags to blocks and plays, and practical examples including NetBox integration for network automation.

top_posts.title: Network Automation Zero to Hero workshop now available
top_posts.summary: The Network Automation Zero to Hero workshop, introduced at AutoCon 2 in Denver, is now available online. The workshop provides a comprehensive guide to implementing a modern intent-based network automation stack, including tools like NetBox, Slurpit, Icinga, Netpicker, Ansible, and ContainerLab. It offers detailed documentation and videos to help users understand and apply key concepts. The course is open-source and community-driven, encouraging users to contribute and extend its functionality.
